AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The count matches (CardsVar(5), PaelsTooth.cs:55, read via DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue at :83, vs CARDS = 5 at paels_tooth.py:18; no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file) and removing the picks from the deck matches (`CardPileCmd.RemoveFromDeck(item)` vs `run.deck.remove(card)`). What diverges is the CANDIDATE FILTER (G1, LIVE -- C# requires IsUpgradable, the sim does not) and the STORED ORDER (G2, LIVE for RNG parity -- C# sorts by card id before storing, the sim keeps selection order). C#'s `item.MutableClone()` (line 86) has no sim counterpart, which is safe here and is N1.

AfterCombatEnd.rationale: PaelsTooth.cs:93-114: bail unless `!base.Owner.Creature.IsDead && SerializableCards.Count != 0` (line 95, mirrored by paels_tooth.py:34's `if run.is_dead or not self.stored_cards: return`); pick with `base.Owner.PlayerRng.Rewards.NextItem(SerializableCards)` (:99), which paels_tooth.py:38 matches exactly via `run.player_rng.rewards.next_item(self.stored_cards)`; upgrade behind `if (cardModel.IsUpgradable)` (:105-108), which paels_tooth.py:42-43 mirrors with `if card.is_upgradable` -- so PROMPT.md bug class 14 does NOT fire here, unlike astrolabe and bone_tea; add to the Deck pile (:109) via run.add_card, which dispatches the same ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck and AfterCardChangedPiles hooks (run.py:341-354) and appends, matching CardPileCmd.Add's default CardPilePosition.Bottom. Two orderings differ harmlessly: C# adds the card then removes it from the store (:109, :111) while the sim removes first (:41), and C# sets base.Status from the PRE-removal count (:110) -- both presentation/bookkeeping with the same end state. C#'s `RunState.ContainsCard` guard (:101) exists because FromSerializable builds a NEW CardModel that must be registered with the run; the sim returns the very Card object it removed, so there is nothing to register twice. The dispatch condition differs in a way that cannot be observed: run.py:1206 skips the hook when `self.is_dead`, and the C# body's own first guard is `!IsDead`.

AfterCloned.rationale: PaelsTooth.cs:75-79 blanks _serializableCards on a model clone, so the canonical/preview copy of the relic never shows another player's stored cards. This is the source's canonical-vs-mutable model infrastructure; the sim has no model-cloning layer and constructs relics directly (relics/base.py:73-74). Infrastructure, no observable effect.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the candidate filter. C# selects from `IsRemovable AND IsUpgradable`; the sim selects from `removable_cards()` alone, so Curses and already-upgraded cards can be stored
guards.issue: MECHANISM: PaelsTooth.cs:83 calls `CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForRemoval(..., filter: (CardModel c) => c.IsUpgradable)`, and FromDeckForRemoval itself ANDs `c.IsRemovable` onto the caller's filter (CardSelectCmd.cs:621-625). paels_tooth.py:27 passes `run.removable_cards()` -- IsRemovable only (run.py:360-362, i.e. everything not Eternal) -- so the IsUpgradable half is dropped entirely. Two observables follow: the choice offered to the player is a different set, and a stored non-upgradable card comes back UN-upgraded at combat end (paels_tooth.py:42-43 correctly guards the upgrade), so the relic silently does nothing for that card where C# would never have accepted it. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py tooth-filter`): with a deck of [strike+1, strike, strike, defend, bash, regret], the sim's candidate set is all six and C#'s is four; driving the sim's own after_obtained then stores `[('strike', 1), ('regret', 0), ('strike', 0), ('strike', 0), ('strike', 0)]`. Both sides ported and both halves are ordinary: 35 of 203 ported cards have max_upgrade_level 0 (18 Curse, 14 Status, 3 Quest -- the census in sweep D), Curses are IsRemovable and reach the deck through curse rewards and events, and ANY card smithed at a rest site (run.rest_upgrade, run.py:1112-1119) is at max level and therefore not IsUpgradable. Note the source is deliberately asymmetric here and the sim copied the wrong half: Pael.cs:162-164's OFFER gate counts `c.IsRemovable >= 5` (which paels_tooth.py:20's MIN_REMOVABLE = 5 matches correctly), while the SELECTION filter is IsUpgradable -- so the game can offer the relic and then present fewer than five candidates.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE for RNG parity): C# sorts the stored cards by id before storing them; the sim keeps selection order, and the store is exactly what the Rewards stream indexes into
guards.issue: MECHANISM: PaelsTooth.cs:83 ends with `.OrderBy<CardModel, string>((CardModel c) => c.Id.Entry, StringComparer.Ordinal)`, and the foreach at :84-89 appends to SerializableCards in that order. AfterCombatEnd then draws with `PlayerRng.Rewards.NextItem(SerializableCards)` (:99), so the ORDER of the list determines which card a given RNG index returns. paels_tooth.py:28-30 appends in `run.select_cards` order. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py tooth-filter`): the same five picks store as `[strike+1, regret, strike, strike, strike]` in the sim and `[regret, strike+1, strike, strike, strike]` under an ordinal sort of the ids -- a different card for index 0. LIVE for RNG parity (the conformance runner compares the deck as (id, upgrade_level) pairs, sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:618, so a differently-ordered store surfaces as a deck mismatch on any seed that takes Pael's Tooth), and dormant for RL play, where the store order is merely arbitrary. A SECOND, subtler half: the sim's card ids are lowercase snake_case while `Id.Entry` is the source's uppercase entry name, and StringComparer.Ordinal is byte order -- '_' (0x5F) sorts AFTER 'Z' (0x5A) but BEFORE 'a' (0x61) -- so even a sim-side sort must be performed on the UPPERCASED id to match, the same rule audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json records for StableShuffle tie-breaking (binding rule 3).

guards.what: N1: `item.MutableClone()` before serialising (PaelsTooth.cs:86) -- a full model clone, where the sim stores the live Card object it just removed from the deck (PROMPT.md bug class 17)
guards.rationale: Sweep E (.superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md) lists five shallow-rebuild sites and this is NOT one of them, correctly: the sim keeps the ORIGINAL object, which preserves strictly more per-instance state than a clone would (upgrade level, enchantment, affliction, cost modifiers), so the class-17 failure mode cannot occur. C# needs the clone because it serialises and the original is about to be destroyed by RemoveFromDeck; nothing can then mutate the stored copy. The sim's object is likewise unreachable while stored -- it is out of run.deck, and run.create_combat deep-copies only the deck (run.py:1136). The one residual difference is identity: C#'s returned card is a fresh CardModel from FromSerializable (:100) and the sim's is the same object that left the deck, which matters to nothing the sim models.

guards.what: N2 (PROMPT.md bug class 16): the RNG stream IS named and IS correctly routed
guards.rationale: C# draws on `base.Owner.PlayerRng.Rewards` (PaelsTooth.cs:99) and paels_tooth.py:37-38 passes exactly that stream when the run carries one. Checked because this is the failure mode class 16 warns about and astrolabe N1 filed as a live gap: here the port did NOT default to the shared rng. The `else` branch (paels_tooth.py:39-40, `run.rng.choice`) is the legacy RL path, taken only when `run.rng_set is None`, which is the repo-wide convention for un-parity-wired runs and is not a divergence from the game. No IsAllowed override in PaelsTooth.cs (executed grep over the batch's C# files), so sweep B's cluster excludes this unit.
